newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T dismisses ruling as procedural.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T dismisses ruling as procedural.

text.p: Tobacco to insurance company B.A.T Industries Plc said on Friday a Mississipi court ruling against the tobacco industry was purely procedural.
"It is a purely procedural decision, all the court has done is to decide not to decide the issues now, it is not a decision on the merits of the case at all," said company spokesman Michael Prideaux.

"We are confident that ultimately we will win the case," he added. Brown & Williamson, a subsidiary of B.A.T, has about 17 percent of the U.S. cigarette market and is one of the defendants in the case along with Philip Morris Cos Inc and RJ Reynolds Tobacco Co.
The Mississipi Supreme Court threw out challenges by Governor Kirk Fordice and the tobacco industry that would have kept the $940 million historic case from proceeding to trial on June 2.
It is the first of 22 such suits filed by state attorney generals across the U.S. to recoup Medicaid costs.
But the Mississippi decision does not mean all these other Medicaid cases will now be heard, said Prideaux.
The decision sent the shares of tobacco companies sharply lower, with Philip Morris Cos off $10.75 to $126 on Thursday. In London B.A.T shares were off 16-1/2 pence at 537p in early trade.
